Ben / team — thanks for the draft plan. A few legal points to keep tidy when we hand these over to Medicore procurement: 

- "No-train" wording: we should use explicit operational language rather than vague promises. Suggested phrasing: \"Redwood will not use Customer Content to improve, train, or update any machine learning models used in Redwood's public or internal model catalog, and will not include Customer Content in any datasets for model training, unless Customer provides an express, written opt-in.\"

- Derivative/output rights: propose a clause that grants the customer perpetual, worldwide rights to outputs, and Redwood disclaims ownership of customer-provided prompts. Keep licensing narrow to avoid resale use cases.

- Subprocessors: the inventory is fine; for higher-assurance customers we offer an \"attestation\" letter signed by our Head of Security that lists subprocessors and confirms contractual flow-downs. That can be a separate attachment (medicore-attestation-request.docx).

- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report and our subprocessor flow-down text should be referenced; do not attach SOC report to external email unless Medicore signs an NDA or confirms recipient list. Provide the attestation + ops diagram publicly; offer SOC2 via secure link.

Benjamin — can you confirm the onshore pinning steps are available for a dedicated or private deployment? David, please confirm the exact steps + CS/ops contacts so we can include a short runbook.

If Medicore is comfortable, we can produce the attestation + DPA addendum and return a DocuSign package within 5 business days.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Counsel — Contracts & Privacy, Redwood Inference
